router_distinctions: haiku vs sonnet: If the answer requires reasoning, analysis, or structured output, use sonnet. If it is conversational, factual recall, or a short answer, use haiku. sonnet vs opus: Use opus only when the task involves system-wide thinking, multi-component architecture, or requires holding many constraints simultaneously. Most code tasks are sonnet. read vs write (_r vs _rw): Use _rw ONLY when the user explicitly requests to create, edit, delete, or modify files, run a tool, or execute a scheduled action. Questions about code or asking for suggestions stay in _r even if they mention files. When in doubt: Default to haiku_r. It is better to respond fast with a simpler model than to over-escalate.

tiers.name: haiku_r
tiers.router_label: Casual conversation, simple factual questions, short summaries, translations, dictionary lookups, weather-style queries, small talk, jokes

tiers.name: haiku_rw
tiers.router_label: Running scheduled jobs, invoking tools (reminders, timers, web search), simple file creation, quick one-line edits, toggling settings

tiers.name: sonnet_r
tiers.router_label: Code review, debugging analysis, explaining complex concepts, comparing options, writing structured content (emails, docs), research synthesis, data interpretation

tiers.name: sonnet_rw
tiers.router_label: Editing code files, implementing features, fixing bugs in code, creating scripts, modifying configurations, writing tests, multi-file text changes

tiers.name: opus_r
tiers.router_label: Architecture design, system-level reasoning, complex trade-off analysis, long-form strategic planning, reviewing entire codebases, deep technical research

tiers.name: opus_rw
tiers.router_label: Large-scale refactoring across multiple files, implementing complex features with many moving parts, redesigning system architecture, building new modules from scratch

tiers.name: agent
tiers.description: Multi-agent coordinator for complex multi-step tasks requiring parallel work by multiple specialized agents
